name: Flutter Entertainment plc

profile.description: Flutter Entertainment plc is the world's largest online sports betting and iGaming operator, with brands including FanDuel, PokerStars, Paddy Power, Betfair, Sky Betting & Gaming, and Sisal. FY2025 revenue was $16.38B. In August 2026 Flutter cut its FY2026 revenue guidance midpoint to $17.91B from $18.305B, driven by the US business, and Q2 2026 revenue rose just 3% to $4.33B. Long-time CEO Peter Jackson was succeeded by International CEO Dan Taylor on October 1, 2026, as prediction markets pressure US sports betting share; shares fell about 65% over the past year.

innovation.label: DEVELOPING
innovation.analysis: Track Record (2/3): Flutter built FanDuel into the leading US online sportsbook, a major new revenue stream that helped lift group revenue from $6.04B in 2020 to $16.38B in 2025 [4], though much of that growth came via mergers (Stars Group, Sisal). AI Deployment (1/2): Flutter describes AI-driven pricing and personalization within its 'Flutter Edge' platform strategy [8], but has not quantified AI revenue or savings. Market Share (1/2): FanDuel remains a scale leader, but new CEO Dan Taylor's stated priority is to win back US market share lost to rivals and prediction markets [5][6], so share is no longer clearly gaining. Pipeline (1/2): Management discusses product and market expansion, but the Q2 2026 update cut US revenue guidance to a $7.4B midpoint without naming specific next-generation launches with revenue visibility [1]. R&D Intensity (1/1): R&D of $991M was 6.0% of 2025 revenue [4], high for gambling operators.

inspiration.label: WEAK
inspiration.analysis: Mission Floor (2/4): Flutter's purpose of 'changing the game' for customers through its brands and the Flutter Edge describes what it does but has no deeper purpose beyond entertainment and wagering [8]. Community Impact (1/2): Flutter runs a Positive Impact Plan with safer-gambling investment and tools [8], but UK regulators have repeatedly penalized its brands for failing vulnerable customers, including a GBP 2M Paddy Power/Betfair penalty and a GBP 1.17M Sky Vegas fine for sending free-spin offers to 41,395 self-excluded people [7]. Employee Retention (0/2): No turnover or tenure data was found. Insider Buying (0/2): No meaningful net insider buying was found despite the roughly 65% share-price decline [6].

infrastructure.label: DEVELOPING
infrastructure.analysis: Calculated mechanically on the Growth weighting (raw 6.50/10, rounded to 6). Forward P/E of 12.0, PEG of 0.19, and a 5-year revenue CAGR of 22.1% (2020 $6.04B to 2025 $16.38B, derived from FMP data) all hit their targets [3][4]. Negative ROE of -7.9% and a -4.4% profit margin score zero on two heavily weighted metrics, D/E of 134% scores 0.72, and latest quarterly revenue growth of 3.3% scores 0.78 [3]. Liquidity is ample at about $252M of daily dollar volume.

ai_resilience.label: MODERATE
ai_resilience.analysis: AI Risk Protection (6/9): Flutter's revenue rests on gaming licenses in tightly regulated jurisdictions, scale in marketing, and proprietary pricing and risk management, which AI tools cannot easily replicate [8]. The real disruption pressure in 2026 comes from CFTC-regulated prediction markets rather than AI, which Bloomberg Law said prompted the CEO change [5]; AI-driven personalization could also deepen regulatory scrutiny of problem-gambling targeting [7]. AI Opportunity (0/1): Flutter uses AI in pricing and personalization but discloses no quantifiable AI revenue [8].

infinite_game.summary: Seen through Sinek's lens, Flutter plays a finite game: the business is built on maximizing wagering volume, growth has come from serial mergers, and the 2026 strategy is framed as winning back market share. A CEO change in response to a stock collapse and new competitors shows reactive rather than purpose-led leadership.

just_cause.analysis: Flutter speaks of entertaining customers responsibly, but there is no vision of a better future state that people would sacrifice to advance [8]. Repeated fines for marketing to self-excluded gamblers show that revenue goals override stated values when they conflict [7].

trusting_teams.analysis: Leadership continuity is reasonable: Taylor is a long-tenured insider who ran Paddy Power Betfair from 2018 and the International division from 2020 [6]. No evidence of exceptional psychological safety was found, so this is average.

worthy_rivals.analysis: Management's language is about share: Taylor's mandate is described as winning back US market share from DraftKings and prediction-market entrants [5][6]. No evidence was found of rivals being treated as benchmarks to learn from.

existential_flexibility.analysis: Flutter moved its primary listing to the NYSE and shifted its center of gravity to the US through FanDuel [8]. These are adaptations within the same betting model; there is no evidence yet of a response to prediction markets that would reinvent the business.

courage_to_lead.analysis: Flutter invested through years of FanDuel losses to build US scale, a real long-term bet that paid off in leadership [4]. The 2026 guidance cuts and CEO change were reactions to market pressure, not deliberate sacrifices [1][5].

investment_thesis: Flutter is the global scale leader in online betting, trading at about 12x forward earnings with a 0.19 PEG after a roughly 65% share-price collapse [3][6]. If new CEO Dan Taylor stabilizes US share and FanDuel margins recover from World Cup marketing and tax pressure, earnings could rebound sharply from 2025's GAAP loss [1][4].
thesis_continued: Revenue growth has stalled (Q2 2026 +3%), FY2026 guidance was cut to a $17.91B midpoint, and prediction markets are an unresolved structural threat to US sportsbook economics [1][5]. Combined with a gambling business model, repeated UK problem-gambling penalties, weak Inspiration, and a finite Infinite Game profile, the IOWN score lands at WATCH.
key_catalysts: Q3 2026 results and Taylor's first strategic update as CEO, including a plan for prediction markets [5][6]
Recovery of FanDuel US share and margins after World Cup-driven marketing spend [1]
Low 12x forward P/E and 0.19 PEG leave room for a rerating if guidance stabilizes [3]
key_risks: Prediction markets taking US sports betting share and compressing hold and margins [5]
Rising gaming taxes and regulatory penalties for failures to protect vulnerable customers [7]
Leverage of 134% D/E with negative GAAP earnings and a large Kentucky judgment under appeal [3][7]
